papers.title_in_file: Unsupervised Quantum Anomaly Detection on Noisy Quantum Processors
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Section I, Section III results (text and captions), Section IV summary, Appendix B dataset description
papers.what_it_is: Compares classical and projected-quantum-kernel One-Class SVMs on a synthetic credit card fraud dataset, in simulation and on trapped-ion and superconducting processors.

assertions.value: The authors report that in simulations the quantum rbf models generalized better than the classical counterparts in the small data and high anomaly regime.
quotes: have shown evidence that with a high probability the quantum rbf- models generalized significantly better than the classical counterparts in the small data and high anomaly regime.
assertions.certainty_reason: One study, one synthetic dataset, Section IV.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper's footnote reports the classical rbf-OCSVM also reached a high F1 on the full dataset, so the advantage applies to the subsampled regime.

assertions.value: The authors state the simulations used a 20-dimensional financial dataset and that further research is required across other data regimes, dimensions and train-test set sizes.
quotes: The simulations of our (q)rbf-OCSVM models on our 20dimensional financial dataset
Further research is required to assess their performance across diverse data regimes, including lower and higher dimensions, as well as varying train-test set sizes.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope limit, Section IV.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Sparkov dataset was synthetically generated and has 1 852 394 samples with 22 features, including a fraud label.
quotes: The Sparkov dataset [44] was synthetically generated by the Sparkov Data Generation tool [49]
In total there are 1 852 394 samples with each 22 different features, including the label fraud or non-fraud.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own data source, Appendix B.
assertions.reader_inference: The fraud data are synthetic, not real transactions.

assertions.value: The authors state they demonstrated that the generalization enhancement is robust to hardware noise and finite sampling effects.
quotes: We have further demonstrated that this generalization enhancement is robust to hardware noise and finite sampling effects.
assertions.certainty_reason: Hardware runs on a small subsampled dataset, Section III.B.

papers.title_in_file: Towards an in-depth detection of malware using distributed QCNN
papers.what_it_is: Builds five section-wise QCNNs plus a scoring function for image-based malware detection with eight qubits per QCNN.

assertions.value: The authors report an increase of around 20% in test accuracy and F1-score for the distributed QCNN model over a single QCNN on whole-file images.
quotes: We get an increase of around 20% of our results, both on the accuracy of the test and its F1-score.
we have a drastic increase (around 20%) of both accuracy and F1-score.
assertions.certainty_reason: One study on two malware datasets, Section 3.

assertions.value: The authors state each QCNN uses eight qubits in three layers and is trained over five epochs, and each sub-dataset has 20k benign and 20k malware files.
quotes: Each sub-dataset is composed of 20k benign and 20k malware
Each QCNN is composed of eight qubits (three layers), and is trained over five epochs.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup, Sections 1.1 and 2.1.

assertions.value: The authors state their previous work showed that quantum neural networks do not perform well on image-based malware detection when using a few qubits.
quotes: our previous work showed that quantum neural networks do not perform well on image-based malware detection when using a few qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Attributed to the authors' earlier work.

assertions.value: The authors report that the per-section QCNN results are not very good and are comparable to the QCNN trained on images of entire files.
quotes: We can see that the results by section are not very good, and actually they are comparable to the model where we train the QCNN on the images of the entire files
assertions.certainty_reason: One study, Section 3, Table 1.

papers.what_it_is: Proposes GQSim, parametrized quantum circuits for learning asymmetric similarity between data from different spaces, shown on synthetic toy data.

assertions.value: The authors propose GQSim, quantum networks that learn task-dependent (a)symmetric similarity between data that need not have the same dimensionality.
quotes: We propose using quantum networks (GQSim) for learning task-dependent (a)symmetric similarity between data that need not have the same dimensionality.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines its own method, Abstract.

assertions.value: The authors report that on a synthetic image data set the learned similarity separated the classes, and state they verified this numerically for all points in X.
quotes: Using a synthetic image data set with left and right pixels blocked, we learn the similarity of these images
Numerically we verified that this is not just true for a subset of points in X, but for all points in X.
assertions.certainty_reason: One toy experiment, Section III.B.

assertions.value: The authors report that a reduced graph with edges as little as 1% reproduces the final graph with 100% accuracy.
quotes: a reduced graph with edges as little as 1% reproduces the final graph with 100% accuracy.

papers.title_in_file: Ansatze for Noisy Variational Quantum Eigensolvers (Master thesis, University of Minho)
papers.version_note: File is a master thesis posted as arXiv 2212.04323; author name in file is Mafalda Francisco Ramoa da Costa Alves, dated November 2021.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Section 1.1 to 1.3 intro, searched conclusions and chapter 6 summary lines; chapters 2 to 5 not read in full
papers.what_it_is: Thesis comparing UCCSD-VQE and ADAPT-VQE under noise in simulators and on IBMQ cloud devices, and testing ways to shrink the ADAPT ansatz.

assertions.value: The author reports that for H2 ground state energy, ADAPT-VQE tolerated a 20 times lower shot count, 150 times larger error rates in state preparations and measurements, and 850 times lower coherence times than UCCSD-VQE.
quotes: For H2, as far as ground state energy calculations are concerned, ADAPT-VQE was shown to tolerate a 20 times lower shot count, 150 times larger error rates in state preparations and measurements, and 850 times lower coherence times than UCCSD-VQE.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation with noise models on one molecule, H2.
assertions.reader_inference: The result is for H2 only; the author expects the gap to grow with system size but does not show it.

assertions.value: The author states that UCCSD-VQE (predetermined) and ADAPT-VQE (dynamic) were implemented in simulators and cloud quantum computers, with noise models used to assess the impact of noise sources on convergence.
quotes: Multiple variants of VQE, namely UCCSD-VQE (predetermined) and ADAPT-VQE (dynamic), were implemented both in simulators and cloud quantum computers.
Using noise models, the impact of several noise sources on convergence was assessed.
assertions.certainty_reason: The thesis states its own setup in the Abstract.

assertions.value: The author reports that ansatz manipulation gave up to a 35-fold decrease in the error for a similar circuit depth within the first 10 iterations of ADAPT-VQE.
quotes: resulting in an up to 35-fold decrease in the error for a similar circuit depth within the first 10 iterations of ADAPT-VQE.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation on a few small molecules.

assertions.value: The author reports that when running UCCSD-VQE on IBMQ cloud quantum computers, chemical accuracy is beyond reach.
quotes: Concluding, when running UCCSD-VQE on IBMQ cloud quantum computers, chemical accuracy is beyond reach.
assertions.certainty_reason: One study on IBMQ cloud devices.

papers.what_it_is: Introduces a hybrid quantum-classical perceptron with proved quadratic gains in samples and margin and an expected-error bound, plus simulations.

assertions.value: The paper shows a quadratic improvement over the classical perceptron in both the number of samples and the margin of the data.
quotes: We show a quadratic improvement over the classical perceptron in both the number of samples and the margin of the data.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 4, with proof in Appendix A.1.
assertions.reader_inference: The bound holds under the stated assumptions (linearly separable data, quantum search access).

assertions.value: The authors state the improvement of the statistical complexity is quadratic only if the data supplied to the classical perceptron are provided the same way as for the quantum one.
quotes: The improvement of the statistical complexity is quadratic only if we assume that the data supplied to the classical perceptron are provided the same way that the quantum one.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own qualifier in the discussion.

assertions.value: The authors state the simulations come from a classical computer simulating a quantum algorithm, and report that on the Iris dataset the three quantum perceptrons are about four times slower than the classical perceptron while on the Hard dataset all show an improvement.
quotes: The simulations presented here come from a classical computer simulating a quantum algorithm.
On the Iris dataset, the three quantum perceptrons behave similarly and are about four times slower than the classical perceptron.
For the Hard dataset, however, all the quantum perceptron algorithms shows an improvement over the classical one.

assertions.value: The authors report that in their noise illustration the success probability of the quantum search in a faulty environment decreases rapidly and does not tend to a non-vanishing constant, and state that a rigorous noise analysis is beyond the scope of the work.
quotes: However in a faulty-environment, the success probability decreases rapidly and do not tend to a non vanishing constant
Although a rigorous analysis goes beyond the scope of this work
assertions.certainty_reason: Bit-flip and depolarization illustration, Section 5.2.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Computer Benchmarking: An Explorative Systematic Literature Review
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Section 1, Section 6 discussion, Section 7 conclusion and limitations; Sections 2 to 5 skimmed by search only
papers.what_it_is: Systematic literature review that builds a taxonomy of gate-based quantum computer benchmarks across hardware, software and application levels.

assertions.value: The authors state they reviewed 401 titles and abstracts, identified 175 papers for full-text assessment, excluded 34 more, and selected 141 studies for initial analysis.
quotes: Using inclusion and exclusion criteria, we conducted a double-blind review of 401 titles and abstracts, identifying 175 papers for full-text assessment. Following this stage, an additional 34 papers were excluded, leading to a final selection of 141 studies for initial analysis
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own review method, Section 1.

assertions.value: The authors state they demonstrated that no single benchmark can comprehensively assess all aspects of QC performance.
quotes: we demonstrated that no single benchmark can comprehensively assess all aspects of QC performance
assertions.certainty_reason: Conclusion of one literature review.

assertions.value: The authors state that the literature currently lacks clear definitions and standardized benchmarking methodologies, citing another work.
quotes: Literature currently lacks clear definitions and standardized benchmarking methodologies [10].
assertions.certainty_reason: Attributed to reference 10.

assertions.value: The authors state the review was restricted to universal gate-based QC, so the taxonomy may not generalize to annealing or analog models, and some recent or non-peer-reviewed benchmarks may not have been captured.
quotes: First, our focus was restricted to universal, gate-based QC, excluding alternative paradigms such as quantum annealing or analog quantum simulation.
Second, given the rapid pace of development in the field, some recent or non-peer-reviewed benchmarks may not have been captured
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limits, Section 7.
